title: Review: Electromagnetic spectrum; Doppler effect; Superposition, interference and coherence; Single-slit diffraction; Young's double slit
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Questions: W02-1#N.14, W06-1#N.12, W07-1#N.2, W08-1#N.12, W02-1#N.9b, W06-1#N.8, W07-1#N.6b, W02-1#N.2, W06-1#N.11, W07-1#N.8b, W06-1#N.2b, W07-1#N.9b. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Diffraction
items.clue: Spreading out of a wave as it passes through a gap or around the edge of an obstacle.

items.label: Young's double slit
items.clue: Experiment in which two narrow, close openings give equally spaced bright and dark bands on a screen.

items.label: Principle of superposition
items.clue: States that the resultant displacement where waves overlap is the sum of the individual displacements.

items.label: Wavefront
items.clue: Surface sent out by a source at a steady rate; bunched ahead when the source moves, spread out behind.

questions.stem: In a vacuum, the microwaves in a speed camera have a wavelength of 3.0 cm, and the light from a yellow lamp has a wavelength of 600 nm. How do their frequencies compare?

options.text: The microwave frequency is 5 × 10⁴ times the light frequency, since f rises with λ.
They are equal, because both waves travel at the same speed, c, in a vacuum.
The light frequency is 5 × 10⁴ times the microwave frequency, since f = c/λ.
The light frequency is higher, because light travels faster than microwaves.

questions.explanation: Same c for both, so f ∝ 1/λ. Ratio = (3.0 × 10⁻² m)/(600 × 10⁻⁹ m) = 5 × 10⁴: the light's frequency is that many times higher.

questions.stem: Two dippers vibrating in phase act as coherent sources S₁ and S₂ on a ripple tank, producing waves of wavelength 2.0 cm. Point P is 31.0 cm from S₁ and 37.0 cm from S₂. What kind of interference occurs at P?

options.text: Destructive: the paths are 15.5λ and 18.5λ, not whole numbers of λ
Destructive: the path difference, 3λ, is an odd number of λ
Neither: maxima occur only where P is equidistant from S₁ and S₂
Constructive: the path difference is 6.0 cm, which is 3λ

questions.stem: Predict first. Monochromatic light passes through two very narrow slits and falls on a distant screen, producing a pattern of bright and dark bands. Which explanation accounts for this pattern?

options.text: Light travels straight through the slits, and each bright band is an image of a slit.
Light spreads out from each slit, and the waves from the two slits overlap and interfere.
Light is refracted at the edges of each slit, which bends it into separate bright bands.
Waves from the two slits interfere where they meet, so no spreading at the slits is needed.

questions.stem: Sea waves reach a harbour wall with a 20 m wide entrance. A boat is moored behind the wall, well to one side of the entrance. On day 1 the waves have a wavelength of 20 m; on day 2, 2.0 m, with the same amplitude. On which day is the boat rocked more, and why?

options.text: Day 1: the wavelength is about the width of the gap, so the waves spread widely.
Day 2: shorter waves have a higher frequency, so they carry more energy around the wall.
Neither: the gap is the same width both days, and the gap alone sets the spreading.
Day 2: shorter waves fit through the gap more easily, so more of them pass behind it.

questions.stem: Predict first. Which ranking of the wavelengths of four categories of electromagnetic waves, from longest to shortest, is correct?

Two loudspeakers connected to the same signal generator emit sound in phase at a frequency of 500 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m s⁻¹. At which of these path differences is the sound quiet because of destructive interference?
questions.explanation: λ = 0.68 m, and 1.02 m = 1.5λ, a half-odd number of wavelengths: crest meets trough, destructive.

questions.stem: In a double-slit experiment, light of wavelength 400 nm is replaced by light of wavelength 600 nm, and the pair of slits is replaced by a pair whose separation is half as large. The screen is not moved. Assume small angles. By what factor does the distance between neighbouring bright bands on the screen change?
Predict first. Which statement describes the nature of electromagnetic waves?

options.text: Oscillations of the particles of the medium they travel through, so they cannot cross a vacuum
Oscillating electric and magnetic fields that travel faster in a vacuum the higher their frequency
Streams of tiny charged particles given out by the source, which can travel through a vacuum
Oscillating electric and magnetic fields, perpendicular to each other and to the direction of travel

questions.stem: A 440.0 Hz tuning fork and a second tuning fork are struck together, and a student counts 12 beats in 4.00 s. Which of the following could be the frequency of the second fork?

Two identical slits each have width a, and their centers are a distance d = 3a apart. Monochromatic light passes through them onto a distant screen. Counting outward from the central maximum (order 0), which is the first bright-fringe order that is missing from the pattern?

options.text: None: every order appears, only dimmer

questions.explanation: The envelope's first zero is at a sin θ = λ. With d = 3a, that is d sin θ = 3λ: exactly where the 3rd-order fringe would be, so it is missing.

questions.stem: Two pulses on a rope overlap at point X. At that instant, pulse 1 on its own would displace the rope at X by 2.0 mm downward, and pulse 2 on its own would displace it by 3.0 mm downward. Taking upward as positive, what is the displacement of the rope at X?

Monochromatic light passes through two slits 0.20 mm apart and falls on a screen 1.5 m away. The centres of the two third-order bright maxima, one on each side of the central maximum, are 18.0 mm apart. What is the wavelength of the light?
